meta.title: Paula Magdy — Full-Stack Software Engineer
meta.description: Paula Magdy is an AWS-certified full-stack software engineer in Cairo, Egypt, with production experience across TypeScript (Next.js/NestJS), PHP (Laravel), and Python (Django/Flask) on AWS, Azure, and Huawei Cloud.

hero.headline: Paula Magdy
hero.descriptionLead: I build production platforms across TypeScript, PHP, and Python on AWS, Azure & Huawei Cloud —
hero.descriptionEmph: contributing across data modeling, API design, CI/CD, monitoring, and security — most recently cutting API latency by ~35% and deploy time from ~20 minutes to under 5.

work.label: SELECTED WORK
work.intro1: Production platforms I helped build with cross-functional delivery teams —
work.introEmph: what each one does, what I contributed, and the stack I worked in.

evaluation.name: Submission & Evaluation Platform
evaluation.blurb: Public-facing submission and evaluation platform delivered for a government client, serving applicants, reviewers, and program operators. I contributed across the backend, data layer, and AWS delivery pipeline.

caseStudy.role: Full-Stack Software Engineer · cross-functional delivery team
caseStudy.overview: A government client needed a public-facing platform to run a large-scale public program, with separate flows for applicants, reviewers, and program operators. It had to meet government security and availability requirements at 5,000+ concurrent users.
caseStudy.system: Next.js frontend and NestJS backend over PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM, deployed on AWS (VPC, EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, IAM, Secrets Manager). Container-first pipelines ship Docker images through ECR to ECS via CodeBuild and CodePipeline. Server-side rendering for SEO, a Vitest / React Testing Library / Playwright test pyramid, and structured logging and monitoring in CloudWatch.
caseStudy.contributions: Developed domain-driven NestJS modules and Next.js features for the applicant, reviewer, and operator flows alongside the frontend and backend teams. · Designed and tuned PostgreSQL schemas with Prisma, adding targeted indexes and query optimizations that cut API latency by ~35% under production load. · Implemented JWT authentication, role-based access control, and structured DTO validation across the API surface with the backend team. · Helped move delivery to container-first CI/CD, reducing deployment time from ~20 minutes to under 5. · Added CloudWatch monitoring and structured logging to the services I worked on, and maintained Vitest, RTL, and Playwright coverage.

legal.name: Legal Services Marketplace Platform
legal.blurb: API-first platform connecting clients with lawyers through a request-and-bid workflow, with in-app payments and real-time communication. I worked on the Laravel backend.

caseStudy.overview: Clients needed a structured way to find the right lawyer and agree on a price, and firms needed a backend to receive, bid on, and manage cases. The platform runs a request-and-bid marketplace with payments, real-time chat, voice and SMS, and escalation handling in a single bilingual (EN/AR) product.
caseStudy.system: API-first Laravel backend with Sanctum authentication, attribute-based routing, and self-validating DTOs, administered through a role-based Filament (Livewire) panel. MySQL for relational data and Redis for cache and queues. Laravel Reverb WebSockets for chat, Twilio for voice and SMS, Firebase Cloud Messaging for mobile push, S3 for media, and Paymob for the in-app wallet, payments, and withdrawals. Pest and PHPUnit cover the domain logic.
caseStudy.contributions: Implemented the request-and-bid workflow connecting clients with lawyers, including escalation handling, as transactional Laravel services. · Built the in-app wallet integration with Paymob for payments and withdrawals. · Designed self-validating DTOs and attribute-based routing under Sanctum authentication with the backend team. · Implemented parts of the real-time and messaging layer with the feature team: Laravel Reverb WebSocket chat, Twilio voice and SMS, FCM push, and S3 media storage. · Contributed to the role-based Filament (Livewire) admin panel and the EN/AR localization, and wrote Pest / PHPUnit tests for the workflows above.

mobileApi.name: High-Traffic Mobile Application Backend
mobileApi.blurb: Laravel API and AWS infrastructure behind a mobile app with thousands of active users. I contributed to the data layer, API hardening, and production infrastructure alongside the backend and DevOps teams.

caseStudy.role: Backend Engineer · backend and DevOps teams
caseStudy.overview: A growing mobile app with thousands of active users needed a backend that held latency steady under load, plus a deployment pipeline and monitoring the team could rely on.
caseStudy.system: Laravel REST API on AWS ECS behind an Application Load Balancer, MySQL on Amazon RDS, and static assets on S3 + CloudFront. Deploys run as containers through ECR, CodeBuild, and CodePipeline; secrets live in Secrets Manager, access is IAM-scoped, and CloudWatch carries the alarms.
caseStudy.contributions: Designed normalized relational data models and optimized complex SQL queries, reducing API latency under production load. · Implemented authentication flows and request validation across the API with the backend team. · Provisioned and maintained production AWS infrastructure with the DevOps team: EC2, RDS, S3, IAM, and Secrets Manager. · Set up CloudWatch dashboards and alarms for the API and database tier so the team had a shared view of production regressions.

scoring.name: Scoring & Ranking Platform
scoring.blurb: Platform that runs large-scale scored events for a government client: participant onboarding, results entry, rule-based scoring, ranking, and live leaderboards. I contributed to the NestJS rules engine and the Next.js operator dashboards and onboarding flows.

caseStudy.role: Full-Stack Software Engineer · cross-functional delivery team
caseStudy.overview: Operators were running the events out of spreadsheets: slow scoring, fragile state, and no real-time visibility for participants. The platform replaces that with structured onboarding and results entry, a configurable rules engine, and live leaderboards.
caseStudy.system: Next.js frontend and NestJS backend with a modular rules engine, PostgreSQL via Prisma ORM, WebSockets for live leaderboard updates, and a Docker-based deployment.
caseStudy.contributions: Developed modules of the scoring engine covering participant onboarding, scoring logic, and ranking with the backend team. · Worked on the real-time leaderboard pipeline and the Next.js operator dashboards that consume it. · Contributed onboarding and results-entry flows to the team's shared, responsive component set, replacing spreadsheet workflows with structured forms and validation.

supportBot.name: Serverless Customer-Support Chatbot
supportBot.blurb: Serverless chatbot on AWS Lambda and Amazon Lex, reached over WhatsApp through Twilio, that answers routine support inquiries and hands off to a human agent when confidence drops. I designed and built the Python orchestration and the Lex intent model, drawing on the support team's ticket history.

caseStudy.role: Software Engineer · independent delivery for the customer-support team
caseStudy.overview: Support agents were handling repetitive inquiries by hand: order status, opening hours, common FAQs. The team needed an automated first line of response that answers instantly and escalates cleanly to a human.
caseStudy.system: Event-driven pipeline: Twilio webhook → AWS Lambda (Python) → Amazon Lex for intent recognition and slot filling, with credentials in AWS Secrets Manager and CloudWatch for tracing. Scales to zero between conversations.
caseStudy.contributions: Designed the intent and slot taxonomy from the support team's ticket history. · Wrote the Python Lambda orchestration bridging Lex, Twilio, and the internal support tooling, with secrets in Secrets Manager and CloudWatch logging. · Automated the common request types, with hand-off to a human agent when confidence dropped, cutting manual triage for the support team.

azureDelivery.name: Azure Infrastructure & API Gateway
azureDelivery.blurb: Azure infrastructure, API gateway, and release pipelines for a client-facing application. I independently provisioned the Azure infrastructure, configured API Management as the API gateway, and set up the release pipelines.

caseStudy.overview: A client-facing application needed Azure infrastructure in place, an API gateway fronting its services, and a release process the team could trust before going to production.
caseStudy.system: Azure compute and storage, Azure API Management fronting the service surface, and release pipelines through Azure DevOps with environment gates.
caseStudy.contributions: Provisioned the Azure infrastructure layout — subscriptions, networking, identity, and policy. · Configured Azure API Management: routing, throttling, and key management for the platform's APIs. · Set up the release pipelines and environment gates that moved the application from staging to production.

r1.b2: Developed backend services for government and enterprise platforms serving 5,000+ concurrent users — domain-driven NestJS modules and Laravel APIs over PostgreSQL/Prisma and MySQL — applying targeted indexing and query tuning that cut API latency by ~35% under production load.
r1.b3: Moved deployments to container-first CI/CD — Docker → ECR → ECS via CodeBuild/CodePipeline — cutting deployment time from ~20 minutes to under 5.
r1.b4: Built the request-and-bid marketplace flow with escalation handling and an in-app wallet on Paymob, letting users pay and withdraw funds without leaving the platform.
r1.b5: Delivered real-time and messaging features — WebSocket chat (Laravel Reverb), voice/SMS via Twilio, FCM push notifications, and S3-backed media storage — giving users live chat, calls, and alerts in Arabic and English.
r1.b6: Hardened API layers across multiple products with Sanctum/JWT authentication, RBAC, attribute-based routing, and self-validating DTOs, rejecting unauthorized and malformed requests before they reached business logic.
r1.b7: Provisioned and maintained AWS infrastructure (VPC, EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, IAM, Secrets Manager) for 5+ production environments, and independently designed and ran the Azure API Management layer.
r1.b8: Instrumented services with CloudWatch monitoring and structured logging, and maintained automated test coverage (Pest, PHPUnit, Jest, Vitest) that runs in CI to catch regressions before release.
r1.b9: Built Next.js/React interfaces — onboarding and results-entry flows, role-based admin panels (Filament/Livewire), and live-updating leaderboards — on a shared, responsive component set reused across products.
r1.b10: Independently designed, built, and shipped a serverless Amazon Lex chatbot on AWS Lambda, integrated with Twilio, automating customer-support conversations and cutting the manual triage load on the support team.
r1.summary: Challenge Group is an AWS/Huawei Cloud partner delivering production platforms for government and enterprise clients across Egypt, KSA, and the UAE. Contributed to multiple production platforms as part of cross-functional Agile delivery teams.

r2.b1: Completed a government-sponsored, intensive software-engineering program (~1,200 hours) spanning full-stack development, system design, and cloud deployment.
r2.b2: Built full-stack applications across two backend ecosystems — Node.js/Express and Python (Django, Flask) — with React front-ends, secure REST APIs, structured authentication flows, and role-based access control.
r2.b3: Modeled both relational (SQL) and NoSQL databases, applying normalization and indexing to keep queries efficient as datasets grew.
r2.b4: Containerized services with Docker and deployed to AWS, applying system-design fundamentals and working in Agile sprints from design through delivery.

r3.b1: Built and shipped a production-ready e-commerce storefront in React — a responsive, cross-device UI wired to REST APIs for the product catalog and cart.
r3.b2: Architected a reusable component library with centralized state via React's Context API, removing prop-drilling and keeping catalog and cart state consistent as the product range and traffic grew.
r3.b3: Improved rendering performance and cut page-load times through render optimization and efficient asset loading, keeping large product listings smooth as the catalog scaled.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.a1: Paula Magdy is a full-stack software engineer based in Cairo, Egypt, with 3+ years of experience. An AWS Certified Solutions Architect, he builds production web platforms with cross-functional teams across frontend, backend, cloud, and DevOps — contributing across data modeling, API design, CI/CD, monitoring, and security.
faq.q2: What technologies does Paula Magdy work with?
faq.a2: He builds with Next.js, React, and TypeScript on the frontend; Node.js, NestJS, and Express, plus Laravel (PHP) and Django/Flask (Python) on the backend; PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Prisma ORM for data; and AWS, Azure, Huawei Cloud, Docker, and CI/CD for cloud and delivery.
faq.a3: At Challenge Group — an AWS/Huawei Cloud partner serving government and enterprise clients across Egypt, KSA, and the UAE — he has contributed to multiple production platforms as part of cross-functional Agile delivery teams. His work spans backend services for platforms serving 5,000+ concurrent users, transactional workflows including a request-and-bid marketplace and an in-app Paymob wallet, real-time chat and messaging, Next.js/React interfaces and role-based admin panels, AWS and Azure infrastructure with container-first CI/CD, and a serverless Amazon Lex support chatbot.
faq.q4: Where is Paula Magdy based, and is he open to remote work?
faq.a4: He is based in Cairo, Egypt, and is open to full-stack engineering roles and consulting engagements, including remote work.
faq.q5: What certifications does Paula Magdy hold?
faq.a5: He holds the AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate and AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner certifications, plus Huawei's HCCDP-Solution Architectures and HCCDA-Tech Essentials — alongside a B.Sc. in Computer Science and Information Systems from October 6 University.
faq.q6: How can I get in touch with Paula Magdy?
faq.a6: You can reach him by email at paulamagdy665@gmail.com or through the contact form on this site — he typically replies within 24 hours.
